# Equity Rotations, Cash-Secured Puts, and Gold Dislocations

Report 158 | Published 2025-03-16 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2025-3-16/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/158.json)

Gold accounting, international rotation and option payoffs.

The gold/GDPNow accounting distinction is strong and explicitly correct. The options example explains downside honestly, but its expiration base-rate claim is false. The eight-year gold comparison also changes winner when dividends are included. The five-year forward gold forecast remains open, and the MSTR put can only be scored as a conditional payoff without an execution record.

**Coverage:** All sections read, including the detailed MSTR put example and both retrospective and prospective gold comparisons. The put is modeled conditionally; no executed premium or brokerage outcome is inferred. Repeated international rotation thesis remains linked to original 2024 framing.

## Claims

### 158-C01

**Gold imports distort trade totals.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | empirical |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | gold-import-accounting |
| Source blocks | 9, 13 |
| Thesis family | gold-import-accounting |

Atlanta Fed documents extraordinary bullion/finished-metal imports and the distinction between Census and balance-of-payments classifications. The reported broad distortion is supported.

**Direction:** Supported for the defined proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Evaluate the explanation separately from subsequent price direction.

**Reviewer confidence:** high

**Outcome evidence:**

- [GDPNow gold adjustment](https://www.atlantafed.org/research-and-data/publications/policy-hub-macroblog/2025/04/23/the-switch-changing-conditions-behind-new-gdpnow-model) | Atlanta Fed | 2025-04-23 | Verified in the audit

Unadjusted GDPNow omitted investment-gold treatment before March 6; alternate adjusted model introduced then and became standard April 30. Jan-Feb BOP gold imports averaged $29.1 bn; a straight annualized adjustment could shift forecast 3.6 percentage points, while actual model effect was smaller.
